Team —

I validated the MAP run matrix and sketched the technical plan below. Short summary first, then the concrete acceptance math.

Test harness & environment
- We'll use our internal harness (k6 + custom token-pacing shim) pointed at a dedicated staging cluster configured to mirror the customer's requested US-only region. Dry-run will run on 1x A100-equivalent node; full benchmark will use 4x nodes with autoscaling disabled.
- Token-level pacing: simulated by replaying sample_requests_gfh.json with per-request token sizes; this reproduces TTFT and streaming behavior.

Workload slices (as columns in the MAP)
- Slice A (UI triage): 60-token prompts / 140-token responses, concurrency 6 sessions, target 25 steady QPS, 150 peak; purpose: validate TTFT p95
- Slice B (summary): 800-token context, concurrency 2 sessions, target throughput test (long-run), target sustained tokens/min target 12k tokens/min for 10m window
- Slice C (mixed): mixture 70% Slice A / 30% Slice B at 30 QPS sustained for 5m, used for hybrid behavior (cache effects)

SLOs & acceptance criteria (proposal)
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): Slice A p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 500ms
- Response latency (full response): Slice B p95 <= 1.2s, p99 <= 2.5s
- Throughput: sustained tokens/min >= 12k on Slice B for 10-minute window (failure if below for two consecutive windows)
- Error budget: <0.2% 5xx errors across runs; any auth/timeout errors are immediate fail and must be investigated

Metrics & instrumentation
- We'll capture per-request TTFT, per-token throughput, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and end-to-end latency (client->response complete). All traces instrumented and available in the MAP folder.

Acceptance gate (boolean)
- Pass = all SLOs met in the full benchmark run AND no more than 0.2% transient errors. If pass, we mark the MAP performance section as "Accepted" and move to contractual close (Lauren to manage credits/commit updates).

Resource notes
- Long-context runs will be CPU/GPU memory bound; recommend using q4_0 quantization for Slice B to increase concurrency without heavy perf regression. I'll run a quick A/B for q4_0 vs fp16 in the dry-run.

I'll run the dry-run today at 17:00 UTC and upload the test_results_20261105.csv into the Drive folder. Priyom — please confirm the logging hooks to include token-level telemetry for the customer.

- Vivek
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
